baseline: Host Linux 6.8.0-124-generic, LTP 20260529 prebuilt binary run from /tmp (copied out of the store): passed 19 / failed 0 / broken 0 / skipped 0. personality01 has tcnt = ARRAY_SIZE(pers) = 19 on x86_64 (18 unconditional entries plus PER_LINUX32 under `#if defined(__x86_64__)`), so 19 passes is full coverage, not a truncated count. Each iteration forks (`.forks_child = 1`), and in the child does SAFE_PERSONALITY(pers[i].pers) then asserts (unsigned long)SAFE_PERSONALITY(0xffffffff) == pers[i].pers. So each of the 19 assertions needs exactly two properties from the kernel: (a) personality(v) stores v and returns the *previous* value, and (b) personality(0xffffffff) is a pure query that returns the current value without setting it. Verified both directly against the real kernel with a compiled probe (/tmp/pers01/probe.c) rather than inferring them: `query: set_ret=0 q1=0x4100001 q2=0x4100001 (PER_SVR4=0x4100001)` - the set returned the old value 0, and two consecutive 0xffffffff queries both returned PER_SVR4, proving 0xffffffff neither stored 0xffffffff nor reset anything. All 19 constants are <= 0x9000004 (PER_LINUX_32BIT), well below 0x80000000, so none can be confused with a negative errno return - which matters because LTP's safe_personality (lib/tst_safe_macros.c:115-127) tst_brk's TBROK on any return < 0, not just -1.

impl.also: kernel/src/process/posix_thread/personality.rs:15-25 (getter/setter over the AtomicU32), kernel/src/process/posix_thread/mod.rs:108-109 (the field), kernel/src/syscall/arch/x86.rs:311 (SYS_PERSONALITY = 135), kernel/src/syscall/arch/generic.rs:289 (SYS_PERSONALITY = 92)

root_cause: No defect. sys_personality already implements both properties the test needs. personality.rs:10-12 returns early on the GET_PERSONALITY constant (0xffffffff, defined at line 25) without calling set_personality, which is exactly the pure-query semantics the probe confirmed on Linux; and every path returns `old_personality`, captured at line 9 before any store. The store itself (line 21) is verbatim - `set_personality(personality)` with no masking - so all 19 values, including the ones carrying STICKY_TIMEOUTS/SHORT_INODE/MMAP_PAGE_ZERO/ADDR_LIMIT_32BIT flag bits above PER_MASK, round-trip intact. The ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE branch at lines 14-17 only logs a warning and does not alter the stored value. The syscall is wired up on both x86 and the generic table, so it is not ENOSYS. The pool entry at test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt:1051 is simply stale: personality01 has never been enabled, so nothing ever un-commented it, and it appears to have been commented out wholesale with the rest of the ~1000 never-enabled entries rather than in response to an observed failure.
asterinas_run: make run_kernel AUTO_TEST=conformance CONFORMANCE_TEST_SUITE=ltp CONFORMANCE_TEST_SELECTOR=personality01 at base commit e8f2b9ca6 (worktree /root/asterinas/.worktrees/run-KgPVlh): `personality01: pass (0.097s)`, TEST SUMMARY Runs 1, Passed 19, Failed 0, Broken 0, Skipped 0, and `All conformance tests passed.` The run used the default CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/tmp with an empty CONFORMANCE_TEST_EXTRA_BLOCKLISTS, which is the correct configuration for an all.txt entry and the one phase 4 will verify. Passed 19 matches the host's 19 exactly, so the kirk-undercount caveat does not bite here: host output is 1582 bytes, under the ~2KB threshold at which the Summary block is lost, and in any case the fallback stdout.count("TPASS") would also be 19 since there are 19 TPASS lines and no TCONF/TSKIP to mis-bucket. qemu.log carries only kirk's aggregate, not the per-TPASS lines, so the 19/0 summary plus the matching host run is the evidence.
invariant: personality(2) stores its argument as the calling thread's personality verbatim and returns the value in effect before the call; the sentinel argument 0xffffffff is a query that returns the current personality and stores nothing. No bits are masked off on the way in, so flag bits above PER_MASK survive a store/query round trip.
linux_reference: Verified empirically against the running host kernel with /tmp/pers01/probe.c rather than by reading source, because every web fetch from this container is blocked (elixir.bootlin.com, git.kernel.org, man.archlinux.org, manpages.ubuntu.com and www.kernel.org all refused). Probe results: 0xffffffff is a pure query returning the current value (two consecutive queries both returned PER_SVR4); personality() returns the previous value; personality IS inherited across fork (child saw 0x6 after the parent set PER_BSD); and personality IS preserved across execve (0x5000002 = PER_SVR3 after execl). Linux keeps the field in task_struct and the syscall lives in kernel/exec_domain.c - the same location the Asterinas comment at personality.rs:20 already cites for the 'accepts any value except the query value' rule.
other_callers: Nobody else reads or writes the personality field: grepping personality across kernel/ and ostd/ finds only the syscall, the getter/setter pair, the field declaration, the two syscall-table entries, and the AtomicU32::new(0) initialiser. Nothing in the kernel branches on personality to change behaviour, so ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE, ADDR_LIMIT_32BIT, MMAP_PAGE_ZERO and friends are stored and reported but never acted upon. That is invisible to personality01, which only checks the round trip.
latent_divergence_out_of_scope: Confirmed real but not exercised by this test, so not a reason to hold the entry back: Asterinas does not inherit personality across fork/clone. kernel/src/process/posix_thread/builder.rs:208 hardcodes `personality: AtomicU32::new(0)` and no clone or exec site ever copies the parent's value, which is what the FIXME at personality.rs:7-8 is about. The probe shows real Linux does inherit it. personality01 cannot catch this because each child calls SAFE_PERSONALITY(pers[i].pers) itself before querying, so it never depends on what it inherited. Fixing it would mean threading the parent's value through PosixThreadBuilder in the clone path; that belongs in its own change, not in the commit that enables this test.
suggested_direction: No kernel change. Enable the test by uncommenting test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt:1051 (`# personality01` -> `personality01`), leaving line 1052's `# personality02` untouched since that test was not diagnosed here.
